newsitem.title: USA: Henkel seen raising Loctite bid. [CORRECTED 22:10 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Henkel seen raising Loctite bid. [CORRECTED 22:10 GMT]

text.p: German consumer products maker Henkel KGaA is likely to boost its $1.2 billion hostile bid for U.S. adhesives maker Loctite Corp once again before a deal is feasible, analysts said on Wednesday (corrects from Tuesday).
Henkel raised the offer to $57.75 a share from $56 on Wednesday and Loctite said a special panel of its board of directors was weighing the bid.
Shares of Hartford, Conn.-based Loctite rose 3/4 to 58-5/8 in early-afternoon trade after Henkel increased its bid to acquire the 65 percent of the company it did not already own.
The trading price of the shares "is clearly above the price that's been put on the table," said David Liebowitz, a managing director at Burnham Securities.
"That leads one to the conclusion that there are clearly investors out there who believe that a better bid may be forthcoming."
Wall Street sources said that any increase was unlikely to be large. "I wouldn't look for big moves from here," said a financial source with knowledge of the deal.
Henkel unveiled its latest offer as a hostile tender earlier Wedneday. The company emphasized it would still like to do a deal on friendly deal on negotiated terms.
Henkel also said its bid conforms with terms of a "permitted offer" under Loctite's shareholder rights plan.
Loctite, meanwhile, urged shareholders to wait for a special board committee recommendation on the offer.

Bob Bartels, an analyst with William Blair & Co in Chicago, said in similar takeover bids the target company would accept a slightly higher price per share, perhaps $1, after balking at an earlier offer.
"My guess is that it will play out in that context," he said. "I think the offer that is on the table is a fairly reasonable offer."
Analysts said the takeover was likely to go through since Henkel has long had the 35 percent stake in Loctite and three of the 12-member board are from the German company.
"It's more of a nudge along than a hostile takeover," the financial source said, adding, "It is Henkel's deep desire to end up with a friendly deal."
Bartels said the merger would provide Henkel, already a world leader in adhesives and sealants, diversity in products and increase its presence in the U.S. market.

The companies set conditions two years ago on a Henkel bid for the rest of Loctite. Under the agreement, Henkel must bid for 100 percent of the stock, make the offer valid for 60 days and end up with at least 50 percent of the stock.
A source close to Henkel said the company had arranged a $1.2 billion bridge loan to help fund the takeover offer. Dresdner Bank is arranging the credit.
